evidence: The task reads as authored for this product, not as a renamed copy. instruction.md opens with a specific client problem: 'Kittle & Rowe is a small law firm, and our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last.' It names two domain-native priorities, ethical walls ('when someone here has a conflict on a matter, they must not learn anything about it, from any corner of the app') and retention with legal hold ('anything a partner has put on legal hold has to survive whatever the timer says'). The notes carry that domain through. walls-and-retention.md has partner/associate/client roles, Dev Anand walled from M-12, a wall that can be added mid-matter and takes effect in open tabs, timers of off/1/7/30 days measured against a fixed firm clock, holds scoped to exactly one message, and transcripts as 'our record of a matter'. The seed kittle.json uses matter ids (M-11 'Pryce lease dispute') and K-n message ids. The template's CHANGE_ME placeholders are fully replaced. Sibling comparison: the only other messaging task in projects/ is threadline-chat (webdev/threadline-chat, category web-development), a Slack-style workspace. Its distinctive surfaces (channels, DMs, reactions, pins, presence/typing, incoming webhooks, append-only audit, pagination, logout revocation) are absent from Kittle. Kittle's core (matter-scoped client visibility, ethical walls on every side channel, disappearing timers, legal hold overriding timers, transcripts, fixed-clock ordering) is absent from Threadline. Of Kittle's 17 functional criteria (judge.toml: signin_and_client_scope, wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live, nested_replies, deleted_and_expired_seed_messages, timer_changes, deleted_message_takes_its_versions, hold_scope_and_release, edits_and_stale_edit, safe_formatting, message_links, unread_and_new_messages_line, sent_once_in_order, live_updates_keep_my_work, search_and_transcript, persistence), about 9 are law-firm-specific. The overlapping ones (stale edit refusal, idempotent send, unread, mentions, live updates, persistence) are generic chat mechanics, and Kittle reframes them in its own domain: unread hidden for walled matters, mentions blocked across walls, deletion that removes versions and quotes. Its flows and criteria are not Threadline's flows with renamed entities. No other sibling (hireops, torquebay, docketlight, drawbill, etc.) is a messaging product. Domain plan: task.toml category = 'Messaging & Chat Interfaces', arena_slice 'full-stack-express-sqlite-messaging-chat-kittle-matter-chat', and keywords match the build-context directive (KITTLE_BUILD_CONTEXT.txt:12 'Keep task.toml category = "Messaging & Chat Interfaces" (as in v1)'). Section 4 of the build context grounds the design in researched messaging failure modes (Matrix MSC3912 edit leakage, Mattermost permalink-preview CVE, Rocket.Chat XSS), which the task authors into law-firm requirements. I found no formal suite-wide domain-plan document beyond that directive, so 'fits the domain plan' was checked against the build context and sibling categories. Adversarial probes for this row: a weak app cannot pass or fail on distinctness. A conforming alternative build is not penalized by anything this row governs. A plausible failure mode would be Kittle as a Threadline reskin, and the criterion and requirement inventories refute it. Workbook and internal-sheet wording match the skill reference. No runtime evidence is required for this row.
